name: CHAPS High-Value Payment — Property Purchase Completion

dependency_notes.JRN-001: Customer (ENT-001) and Account (ENT-004) must exist with status = active. PER-001 must be authenticated.
dependency_notes.JRN-006: MortgageAccount (ENT-016) must exist for the property. Mortgage completion instruction from solicitor drives the payment amount and beneficiary.

business_context: A personal customer (PER-001) instructs a CHAPS high-value payment to a conveyancing solicitor's client account on property purchase completion day. The payment is typically £100k–£2m (property purchase price less mortgage advance already released by lender). CHAPS settles same-day via Bank of England RTGS (RT2 infrastructure, live April 2025), is irrevocable once settled, and must be submitted before the CHAPS daily cut-off (16:00 for customer-initiated payments). ISO 20022 enhanced data obligations apply: LEIs for corporate beneficiaries and Purpose Codes are mandatory from 1 May 2025 (GOV-003-R03). Confirmation of Payee (CoP) check is mandatory before submission (GOV-003-R02). Real-time sanctions screening is required (GOV-005-R02).

phases.name: Payment Initiation
phases.description: PER-001 logs into online banking (CH-001) or mobile app (CH-002) and initiates a CHAPS payment. They enter beneficiary sort code, account number, payment amount, payment reference, and intended completion date. The channel performs client-side validation (format checks, amount range). A PaymentIntent is created in SVC-001 with payment_rail = CHAPS.
entry_conditions: PER-001 is authenticated (SCA — two-factor) in the channel
Account.available_balance >= payment amount (pre-check; definitive check at PH-079)
Payment date = today (CHAPS is same-day only)
exit_conditions: payment_rail = CHAPS confirmed on PaymentIntent record

required_fields: amount_gbp (positive decimal, max 2dp, no statutory maximum for CHAPS)
purpose_code (ISO 20022 Purpose Code — mandatory for property: GDDS = goods and services purchase or PROP = property purchase)
chaps_specific_data.amount_threshold: No regulatory maximum. Bank policy: amounts ≥ £10,000 flagged for enhanced real-time monitoring. Property purchase range typically £100k–£2m.

phases.name: Confirmation of Payee Check
phases.description: SVC-009 proxies a CoP request to the Pay.UK CoP service to verify that the beneficiary name matches the account at the receiving bank. Result (match | partial_match | no_match | unavailable) is returned to the channel. For property transactions, a no_match result requires explicit customer confirmation with fraud risk warning. CoP is mandatory for all CHAPS payments (GOV-003-R02).
entry_conditions: Beneficiary sort code and account number captured
exit_conditions: CoP result received and recorded on CHAPSPaymentIntent.cop_result
If no_match: PER-001 has explicitly confirmed intent to proceed (logged for audit)
If match or partial_match: proceed automatically after customer review

phases.name: Sanctions Screening
phases.description: SVC-014 (KYC/AML) orchestrates real-time sanctions screening of the CHAPS payment beneficiary (account name, account details) against OFSI/UN/EU sanctions lists via SVC-051. This is a hard gate — the payment cannot proceed until sanctions screening returns a clear result. Same sanctions screening pattern as JRN-002 but for CHAPS rail. Property transactions carry elevated AML risk (GOV-003 context: property purchases are a common money laundering vector).
entry_conditions: CoP result is not blocking (PER-001 has confirmed if no_match)
exit_conditions: SanctionsScreeningCompleted (EVT-P02 reused) published with result = clear OR
phases.sla: Sanctions screening must complete within 3,000ms (GOV-005-R02 hard limit)

phases.name: Payment Authorisation
phases.description: PER-001 reviews the full payment summary (beneficiary details, CoP result, amount, purpose code, CHAPS cut-off warning if < 30 minutes remaining) and provides strong customer authentication (SCA) to authorise the payment. For amounts ≥ £10,000, the channel displays an enhanced confirmation screen with irrevocability warning. The channel calls CAP-003 API to confirm authorisation.
entry_conditions: PER-001 has reviewed CoP result and beneficiary details
Current time is before CHAPS customer cut-off (16:00)

phases.name: CHAPS Submission and Settlement
phases.description: SVC-009 constructs and submits an ISO 20022 pacs.008 CHAPS message to the Bank of England RTGS (RT2). The message includes mandatory ISO 20022 enhanced data: Purpose Code (PROP for property purchase) and structured address fields. For corporate beneficiaries, LEI is included (mandatory from 1 May 2025). SVC-009 monitors the RTGS submission for acceptance or rejection. On acceptance by RTGS, the payment is settled — irrevocable. Settlement typically occurs within minutes on a business day during CHAPS operating hours. SVC-001 debits the customer account on receipt of CHAPSPaymentSettled.
entry_conditions: Current time is before CHAPS bank cut-off (internal technical cut-off, earlier than customer cut-off)
exit_conditions: CHAPSPaymentSettled (EVT-111) published — RTGS acceptance confirmed, funds irrevocably transferred
MortgageCompletionPaymentConfirmed (EVT-112) published — notifies JRN-006 mortgage completion flow

chaps_message_fields.purpose_code: PROP (Property Purchase — mandatory for property completion payments)
chaps_message_fields.structured_address: Required from November 2026 (GOV-003-R03 Phase 2); unstructured accepted until then
chaps_message_fields.lei_requirement: Mandatory for corporate beneficiaries from 1 May 2025 (GOV-003-R03 Phase 1); not required for individual solicitor client accounts in this scenario unless the beneficiary is a legal entity

phases.name: Completion Confirmation and Notifications
phases.description: Following successful CHAPS settlement, the customer is notified via push notification, email, and in-app confirmation. The payment appears immediately in the transaction history. The mortgage completion is confirmed to SVC-002 (Mortgage Service) via async event, enabling it to update MortgageAccount status to completed. An audit record is created in the WORM pipeline.

happy_path.description: PER-001 initiates CHAPS payment before cut-off. CoP returns match. Sanctions screening returns clear. PER-001 authorises with SCA. RTGS accepts and settles the payment. Customer and mortgage completion notified.

alternative_paths.name: CoP Partial Match — Customer Proceeds
alternative_paths.description: CoP returns partial_match (name differs slightly — e.g. middle name absent). Channel displays partial-match warning with beneficiary details. PER-001 reviews and confirms intent to proceed. Payment continues to PH-079.

alternative_paths.name: CoP No Match — Customer Proceeds with Explicit Confirmation
alternative_paths.description: CoP returns no_match. Channel displays high-prominence fraud risk warning (GOV-003-R02). PER-001 must check beneficiary details with their solicitor, then explicitly confirm intent to proceed. Explicit confirmation is logged for audit (Consumer Duty GOV-003-R02 evidence). Payment continues to PH-079.

alternative_paths.name: CHAPS Cut-Off Warning — Same-Day Urgency
alternative_paths.description: PER-001 initiates payment within 30 minutes of CHAPS customer cut-off (16:00). Channel displays cut-off warning. If PH-080 authorisation completes before cut-off, payment is submitted. If authorisation misses cut-off, payment cannot be submitted today — customer is advised to retry next business day.

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Hit — Payment Blocked
exception_paths.description: SVC-051 returns a sanctions match during PH-079. EVT-006 (SanctionsHitDetected) is published. SVC-001 blocks the PaymentIntent. MLRO is alerted. PER-001 is informed the payment cannot be processed (generic message — tipping-off prohibition applies). Payment is not submitted to RTGS.

exception_paths.name: Insufficient Funds — Payment Rejected
exception_paths.description: Definitive available balance check at PH-080 reveals insufficient cleared funds. PaymentIntent.status = rejected. Customer notified. No CHAPS submission.

exception_paths.name: RTGS Rejection — Technical Failure
exception_paths.description: Bank of England RTGS rejects the pacs.008 message (e.g. invalid message format, scheme rule violation). SVC-009 receives RTGS rejection. CHAPSPaymentFailed (EVT-113) is published. SVC-001 releases the reserved funds. Customer notified with explanation and guidance to resubmit or contact the bank.

exception_paths.name: Missed CHAPS Cut-Off
exception_paths.description: Payment is authorised in PH-080 but CHAPS bank cut-off passes before SVC-009 can submit the pacs.008. CHAPSPaymentFailed (EVT-113) published with reason = cut_off_missed. Reserved funds released. Customer advised to resubmit on the next business day. Particularly critical for property completions — customer must be warned of legal consequences of missing completion.

design_decisions.decision: CHAPS is handled within SVC-009 (Domestic Payments, CAP-003) as a retained sub-capability. No separate CHAPS service is introduced.
design_decisions.rationale: CAP-003.03 (CHAPS) promotion test yielded 0 criteria met (see payment-operations.json DD-004). SVC-009 already handles FPS and BACS rails. CHAPS is an additional rail within the same service, using the same Form3/Bottomline PTX connectivity layer with a different message format (ISO 20022 pacs.008 to RTGS vs pacs.008 to Vocalink).
design_decisions.rejected_because: Promotion criteria not met. CHAPS shares the same payment execution lifecycle and operational team.

design_decisions.decision: CHAPSPaymentExecution is a new entity (ENT-052) separate from ENT-009 (PaymentExecution) which covers FPS.
design_decisions.rationale: CHAPS execution carries additional required fields not present in FPS: ISO 20022 purpose_code, structured_address, LEI, RTGS message reference (UETR), and settlement_status (RTR2 specific). Extending ENT-009 would create a sparse entity with many nullable fields. A separate entity with explicit CHAPS fields is cleaner and easier for future RTGS compliance changes.
design_decisions.rejected_because: FPS and CHAPS have diverging compliance data requirements. ENT-009 extension would accumulate technical debt as CHAPS ISO 20022 enhanced data obligations evolve (GOV-003-R03 Phase 2 November 2026).

design_decisions.decision: MortgageCompletionPaymentConfirmed (EVT-112) is published by SVC-009 (not SVC-001) and consumed by SVC-002 (Mortgage Service).
design_decisions.rationale: SVC-009 owns the definitive CHAPS settlement fact (CHAPSPaymentExecution.settlement_status = settled). SVC-002 requires this event to transition MortgageAccount.status to completed. The event crosses the CAP-003 → CAP-001 boundary and must flow via the Event Bus (SVC-102). SVC-009 publishes the event because it has the authoritative settlement confirmation from RTGS.
alternatives_considered: SVC-001 publishes the event after AccountDebited
SVC-002 polls SVC-001 for account debit confirmation
design_decisions.rejected_because: SVC-001 debit is a consequence of settlement, not the settlement itself. Polling would violate the async-first cross-capability communication rule.
